item.title: $1.04 billion Powerball jackpot won in Illinois
item.description: A single ticketholder in Illinois won a Powerball jackpot of $1.04 billion Wednesday night, the game says.

item.title: Trump says U.S. has "total control" over Strait of Hormuz
item.description: President Trump said Wednesday that the U.S. has "total control" over the Strait of Hormuz, writing on social media: "I THINK WE WILL KEEP IT."

item.title: Student shot during argument in Georgia high school bathroom, officials say
item.description: An argument in the bathroom of a high school in Warner Robins, Georgia, ended with one student shot and another in custody, officials said.

item.title: Trump says Secret Service wanted him on a "different plane," new details on switch emerge
item.description: CBS News' Olivia Rinaldi has new details on the news that President Trump and other government officials took extraordinary air security measures amid threats from Iran.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy says "I can't do it," breaks down during medical examiner's testimony
item.description: The judge in Lindsay Clancy's trial for the killings of her three children had to call multiple breaks on Wednesday as she broke down in tears during testimony about the injuries her children suffered in their deaths. CBS News Boston's Penny Kmitt has more.

item.title: Watch: Total solar eclipse mesmerizes crowds throughout Europe
item.description: On August 12, 2026, a total solar eclipse awed onlookers throughout Europe, including in Spain and the United Kingdom. Video Producer: Martina Di Licosa

item.title: ICE plans to give officers gloves that can deliver electric shocks
item.description: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers may soon be outfitted with gloves that can deliver painful electric shocks that are intended to gain compliance from combative individuals.

item.title: Eclipse chaser on the celestial events: "There is absolutely nothing like it"
item.description: Western Iceland and northern Spain were on the path of totality for a peak eclipse experience on Wednesday. Chris Orion, an eclipse chaser, joins CBS News to discuss from Sasamón, Spain.

item.title: Nick Reiner indicted on murder charges in parents' killings at their LA home
item.description: Nick Reiner pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder with the special circumstance allegations in the killings of his parents, Rob and Michele Reiner.

item.title: U.S. robocalls skyrocket to over 4 billion in July as consumer groups ask FCC to intervene
item.description: Last month consumers received more than 4.3 billion robocalls, according to the robocall protection app YouMail. CBS Newspath correspondent Evyn Moon has more.

item.title: ICE to spend up to $20 million on gloves that deliver painful electric shocks, DHS notice says
item.description: ICE is planning to spend up to $20 million on gloves for its agents that can deliver painful electric shocks, according to a DHS notice. CBS News' Camilo Montoya-Galvez has more on the gloves and CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson discusses some of the constitutional questions that could come from their use.

item.title: Colombia earthquake death toll rises as frantic search for survivors continues
item.description: The devastation has tested Colombia's new president and his government as it scrambles to respond to the disaster and civil society as it pushes to provide aid to the most affected communities.

item.title: Surrogate gives birth to baby at center of multistate legal battle
item.description: Surrogate McKenna West declined to get an abortion requested by the intended parents after the baby she was carrying was diagnosed with a severe but treatable heart defect.

item.title: Hourly workers are "rusting out" on the job amid dissatisfaction, survey finds
item.description: A survey by scheduling software provider Deputy found one in seven hourly workers feel merely "ok" about their jobs, a sign that researchers say can lead to lackluster performance. CBS News' MoneyWatch reporter Megan Cerullo explains the concept of "rusting out."

item.title: What to expect from the 2026 midterm elections after Tuesday's primaries
item.description: More key midterm matchups are set after six states held primaries on Tuesday. CBS News' Jarred Hill reports on the results and CBS News political reporter Zak Hudak breaks down some of the most contentious midterm races unfolding across the country.

item.title: The comeback story of baby elephant after her mother rejected her
item.description: Linh Mai, a baby elephant born at the National Zoo in Washington, D.C., was rejected by her mother. But after the zoo's elephant caretaker and a dozen others stepped in to help her, she has bonded with other elephants. Tony Dokoupil has the story.

item.title: Texas steps in as surrogate delivers baby, despite intended parents seeking abortion
item.description: California parents wanted to end a surrogate pregnancy when doctors diagnosed the baby with a severe heart defect at 20 weeks. The surrogate refused and went to Texas, where the state has now stepped in. The baby was born on Wednesday. Jason Allen reports.

item.title: What is credit card skimming, and how can you protect yourself?
item.description: A form of credit card theft known as skimming is on the rise as thieves install their own card readers to steal your information and money. It's a particular threat to users of EBT cards. Carter Evans reports on how to spot them and protect yourself.

item.title: Europe sees total solar eclipse: "A very grand thing connected to something bigger than yourself"
item.description: A total solar eclipse turned day into night across a slice of Europe and North America on Wednesday, and put millions in unique contact with the heavens above. Meteorologist Rob Marciano reports from Spain.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy sobs in court as medical examiner describes children's injuries before they died
item.description: Lindsay Clancy had an emotional day in court on Wednesday in the trial for killing her three children. She's fighting murder charges, saying she was suffering from postpartum psychosis and overmedication. Shanelle Kaul reports.

item.title: Miraculous rescue gives moment of hope in Colombia after devastating earthquake
item.description: 48 hours after the devastating earthquake in Colombia, its president said the death toll jumped to 181 people, and thousands were still reported missing. Lilia Luciano reports on a rescue effort in a hard-hit city.

item.title: 11 charged for alleged sham marriages to help Chinese nationals get green cards
item.description: The DOJ unveiled criminal charges alleging 11 people participated in a scheme that involved more than 1,000 "sham marriages" between Chinese nationals and U.S. citizens.

item.title: 2 killed as Apache helicopter from Fort Hood crashes in Salado, Texas
item.description: Two soldiers aboard an AH-64 Apache attack helicopter based out of Fort Hood were killed in a crash on Wednesday, according to local authorities and the Army.

item.title: Whole Foods recalls some jalapeño products over salmonella risk
item.description: Certain salsas, guacamole, pico de gallo and prepared jalapeño products at Whole Foods are among the products recalled over possible salmonella risk.

item.title: Trump's secret plane switch took place within a day of credible missile threat
item.description: President Trump secretly moved from Air Force One to another plane within a day of U.S. and Turkish intelligence picking up on an Iranian plot to fire a missile at the jet, CBS News has learned.

item.title: 8/12: CBS Evening News
item.description: Heavy rain triggers flash flood emergencies; two killed in military helicopter crash.

item.title: 8/12: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Key takeaways from Tuesday's primaries in six states; Karoline Leavitt leaving role as White House press secretary.

item.title: U.S. indicts former SPLC executive for her role in alleged fraud scheme
item.description: Prosecutors have accused the Southern Poverty Law Center of telling donors and banks it was dismantling white supremacist and extremist groups, while funneling payments to confidential informants in the groups.

item.title: Stunning photos show total solar eclipse over Europe
item.description: The only total solar eclipse of 2026 crossed the Northern Hemisphere today, with a path of totality across parts of Greenland, Iceland and northern Spain. See photos and video from the best viewing locations.

item.title: Farm linked to cyclosporaisis outbreak went years without FDA inspection
item.description: The FDA has long fallen short of legally required inspection targets, and foreign inspections fell further last year amid agency layoffs.
